usage: Polite-neutral; checking whether a place has a lot

Do you happen to have parking?

usage: Polite-neutral; the standard line at a full-service gas station

The alternative: order a set amount instead of a full tank

Regular gas, fill it up.

가득이요. 카드로 할게요.
Fill it up. I'll pay by card.
Add how you'll pay; 카드로 ('by card') right away saves a step
경유 가득 넣어 주세요. 영수증도 주세요.
Fill it up with diesel, please. And a receipt too.

usage: Polite; telling a passenger you must refuel
반말, to a friend in the car
주유하다 is the more formal Sino-Korean verb for the same thing

Hold on, I need to get gas.
Said before pulling into a station mid-drive
기름 넣어야 돼서 주유소 좀 들를게요.
I need gas, so I'll stop by a station.
들르다 ('to stop by') is the natural verb for a quick gas stop
기름이 거의 없어서 기름 넣어야 돼요. 근처에 주유소 있어요?
I'm low on gas so I need to fill up. Is there a station nearby?

usage: Polite-neutral; checking if you pump your own gas

examples: 여기 셀프예요?
Is this self-service here?
Asked as you pull in, unsure of the pump type
셀프예요? 그럼 어떻게 넣어요?
Is it self-serve? Then how do I pump it?
Follow up with 어떻게 넣어요 ('how do I put it in') if unsure
셀프 주유소가 더 싸요. 직접 넣어야 되지만요.
Self-service stations are cheaper, though you pump it yourself.
직접 넣다 ('pump it yourself') — self-serve trades effort for a lower price

examples: 신호 바뀌었어요, 가도 돼요.

앞에 신호 빨간불이에요, 멈춰야 돼요.
Red light ahead, you need to stop.

신호 바뀌었어요! 뒤에서 빵빵거려요.
The light changed! They're honking behind us.

usage: Polite; telling a passenger to buckle up

usage: Polite; warning a driver to slow down

The reason — 단속 카메라 ('enforcement camera') ahead
examples: 과속하지 마세요. 위험해요.
Don't speed, it's dangerous.
Pair the warning with 위험하다 ('to be dangerous')
여기 어린이 보호구역이에요. 과속하지 마세요.
This is a school zone. Don't speed.
어린이 보호구역 ('child protection zone') — heavily enforced, big fines
앞에 과속 카메라 있어요, 속도 줄이세요.
Speed camera ahead, slow down.

The grammar pattern -지 마세요 is THE way to tell someone not to do something — built on 말다 ('to stop/refrain') — and a top learner error is negating with 안: 과속 안 하세요 means 'you don't speed' (a statement), not the command 'don't speed.' A softer alternative is 천천히 가세요 ('drive slowly') or 속도 줄이세요 ('reduce speed'), which nudge rather than prohibit. usage: More formal; 주차 요금 ('parking charge') + 어떻게 돼요
Asking the per-unit rate when it's metered

How much is parking here?
Asked at the booth or to staff before parking
주차비 얼마예요? 식당 이용하면 할인돼요?
How much is parking? Is there a discount if I eat here?
할인되다 ('to be discounted') — many places validate for customers
주차비 30분에 천 원이에요, 초과되면 10분에 오백 원이고요.

usage: Is it not OK to park here?
Polite; checking if parking is allowed/forbidden
The positive version — asking permission directly
반말, telling a friend it's not allowed
Stating the rule — 주차 금지 ('parking prohibited')
examples: 여기 주차해도 돼요?
Is it OK to park here?
The everyday way to ask before leaving your car
여기 주차하면 안 돼요. 견인돼요.
You can't park here — they'll tow it.
견인되다 ('to be towed') is the consequence of illegal parking
잠깐 세우는 것도 안 돼요? — 네, 여기 주차 금지예요.
Not even for a moment? — No, it's a no-parking zone.
주차 금지 ('no parking') — even brief stops can be ticketed

usage: The general version — 사고 ('accident') of any size
I need to call the insurance company
The next step — calling your 보험 회사
examples: 주차하다가 접촉사고 났어요.
I had a fender-bender while parking.
-다가 ('in the middle of') shows the accident happened during parking
접촉사고 났어요. 많이 안 다쳤어요, 차만 살짝 긁혔어요.
Had a small collision. No one's hurt, just a scratch on the car.
긁히다 ('to get scratched') for minor body damage
접촉사고 났는데 어떻게 해야 돼요? 보험 부를까요?
I had a fender-bender — what should I do? Should I call insurance?
보험 부르다 ('call insurance [to the scene]') is standard in Korea

usage: Polite-neutral; checking the turn with a passenger or nav
Is it a right turn here?
Turn left at the next intersection
Giving the instruction; 사거리 ('intersection') as the landmark
examples: 여기서 좌회전해요?
Do I turn left here?
Asked at a junction when you're unsure
여기서 좌회전해요, 아니면 직진해요?
Do I turn left here, or go straight?
직진하다 ('to go straight') as the other option
여기서 좌회전하면 안 돼요, 비보호예요. 신호 받고 가세요.
You can't just turn left here, it's unprotected. Wait for the green arrow.

These are exactly the words the 내비 (GPS) speaks and the road signs show, so memorize them as a set. The particle is 에서 (contracted to 서 in speech) because the turn is an action happening AT a location: 여기서 ('at here'). A top learner error is using 에 instead — 여기에 좌회전해요 is wrong because the turn is an activity at that spot, not a destination you arrive at. usage: Polite; directing a driver to the electronic-toll lane
No Hi-Pass? Take the regular lane
일반 차로 ('regular lane') where you pay cash/card
통행료 ('toll') + 내다 ('to pay') at the manned booth
examples: 하이패스 있어요? 그럼 하이패스로 가세요.
Got Hi-Pass? Then take the Hi-Pass lane.
Check for the device first, then direct them
하이패스로 가세요. 안 멈춰도 돼요.
Take the Hi-Pass lane — you don't have to stop.
안 멈춰도 되다 ('don't need to stop') is the whole point of Hi-Pass
하이패스 단말기 없어서 일반 차로로 가야 돼요. 통행료 현금으로 내도 돼요?
No Hi-Pass unit, so I have to use the regular lane. Can I pay the toll in cash?
단말기 ('the device') + paying 통행료 by 현금 ('cash')
